newsitem.title: UK: Centrica down on stock overhang.
newsitem.headline: Centrica down on stock overhang.

text.p: Shares in Centrica Plc dropped in heavy trading on Tuesday amid gloomy analyst comment on the stock's valuation and talk of a large overhang of stock in the market, dealers said.

Extending Monday's decline after the company was spun off from British Gas Plc, the shares were down 2-1/2p at 62-3/4 in volume of 46 million shares -- boosted by some 30 million in large block trades.
Dealers said there was talk that former U.S. holders of British Gas ADRs were looking to sell the stock, which has no U.S. listing.

"The rumour is that there is a massive overhang of as much as 150 million shares from the ADR holders," said the head of equity trading at one top brokerage, "but I don't think it is as large as that and I think the stock will rally once any ADR selling has cleared."
Another market-maker added: "The stock has had a bad press but we are seeing a couple of decent buyers...and we have not seen any ADR sellers."
Yesterday Centrica, which owns the pipeline network and the exploration operations of the former British Gas Plc, dropped 10-1/4p from their "grey market" price on their official debut.
Merrill Lynch put a fair value of just 40p on the stock, which will not pay a dividend for some time.
Meantime BG Plc, also spun off from British Gas, was up 1-1/2p at 176 in volume of 11.5 million shares.
